locator: fn1
excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems.
paraphrase: Footnote defines catastrophic risk as the most severe potential AI harms, such as existential threats or global destabilization.

locator: fn1
excerpt: We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
paraphrase: The term catastrophic risk is used in its plain meaning, not a statutory definition.

locator: fn1
excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
paraphrase: Statutory definitions such as California SB 53's are handled through separate compliance frameworks.

excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: This section presents recommendations for industry-wide measures to keep catastrophic risk low amid rapid AI progress.

excerpt: We lay this out in a three-column table.
paraphrase: The recommendations are presented in a three-column table.

excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations.
paraphrase: The left column of the table lists capability thresholds requiring heightened mitigations.

excerpt: The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
paraphrase: The middle column summarizes planned mitigations detailed further in the Roadmap and elsewhere in the policy.

excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
paraphrase: The right column contains the industry-wide safety recommendations for each threshold.

excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
paraphrase: The company/industry-wide distinction reflects that a single developer cannot ensure industry-wide safety alone.

excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to the industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
paraphrase: The recommendations will nonetheless shape important aspects of Anthropic's work, as detailed below.

locator: bullet 1
context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work.
paraphrase: The recommendations serve as the guiding standard for risk mitigation planning and public policy work.

locator: bullet 1
context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to advance these recommendations through example-setting, technical work, industry advocacy, and policy advocacy.

locator: bullet 2
context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted competitor-contingent commitments to follow the recommendations when confident other developers do likewise.

excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot currently specify in detail the evaluations for passing risk thresholds or the mitigations needed.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
paraphrase: The recommendations rely on requiring safety-case analysis and argument rather than fixed AI Safety Levels.

excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for.
paraphrase: This structure allows flexibility in threshold evaluation and safety argumentation.

excerpt: But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
paraphrase: This flexibility creates a challenge because views on adequate risk assessment and mitigation may differ across actors.

excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
paraphrase: Anthropic suggests third-party governance of all frontier developers as the best implementation path, determining who must provide risk analyses and judging their adequacy.

excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
paraphrase: Countries should harmonize national regulation and evidentiary standards to avoid a race to the bottom.

excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality standards for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could voluntarily review and enforce quality standards for private AI developers.

locator: fn2
excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
paraphrase: A single analysis could cover a broad model category rather than requiring per-release analyses.

locator: fn2
excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
paraphrase: Determinations of which developers must provide analysis should try to spare smaller developers unnecessary compliance burden.

excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations.
paraphrase: The industry-wide recommendations are expected to evolve significantly as knowledge improves.

excerpt: We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic hopes the recommendations become more specific over time.

context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: AI systems with the ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with serious potential for catastrophic damages.
paraphrase: The threshold is met when AI systems can significantly help individuals with basic technical backgrounds create or deploy chem/bio weapons capable of catastrophic damage.
stated_bar: basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees)

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We will maintain or improve on our ASL-3 protections, which include classifier guards at least as robust as our initial Constitutional Classifiers; access controls for trusted users with exemptions to classifier guards; red-teaming, bug bounties, and threat intelligence for continually assessing the threat of jailbreaks; and a number of noteworthy security controls.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to maintaining or improving ASL-3 protections including classifier guards, access controls, and ongoing red-teaming/threat intelligence.

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: Specifics may change, but we will maintain equally or more robust measures over time and will publish updates in our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Specific measures may evolve but will remain equally or more robust, with updates published in Risk Reports.

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We expect to continuously meet the criteria in the right column, although we cannot make guarantees about an evolving landscape with continually adaptive attackers.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to continuously satisfy the industry-wide criteria but cannot guarantee this given adaptive attackers.

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that individual users and relatively small teams will not become significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: Frontier developers should argue convincingly that small teams/individuals won't gain significantly increased ability to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. This will likely require:
excerpt: Restrictions on model behavior, and/or measures for quickly detecting and acting on Usage Policy violations, accompanied by a strong case that these measures are difficult to reliably, sustainably circumvent via jailbreaking.
paraphrase: Recommended measures include behavior restrictions or rapid detection/response to policy violations, with a strong case against reliable jailbreak circumvention.

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. This will likely require:
excerpt: Precautions against opportunistic theft of model weights, such as centralized controls on third-party applications and software updates.
paraphrase: Recommended precautions include centralized controls on third-party apps and updates to prevent opportunistic weight theft.

locator: Table / Non-novel chemical/biological weapons production / footnote 3

paraphrase: This threshold covers AI systems that could significantly help expert-backed teams create chem/bio weapons more catastrophic than COVID-19.

locator: Table / Novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We will apply protections at least as strong as our ASL-3 protections (see previous row) to an expanded set of potential use cases for AI, covering the most likely vectors for this threat.
paraphrase: Anthropic will extend ASL-3-level protections to cover a broader set of use cases relevant to this threat.

locator: Table / Novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: Additionally, we will identify the most concerning specific threat pathways, create policy recommendations for early detection and response for such threats, and share this content with policymakers.
paraphrase: Anthropic will identify key threat pathways, create early-detection policy recommendations, and share these with policymakers.

locator: Table / Novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that threat actors will not become significantly more likely to cause the sort of catastrophic harm discussed in the lefthand column via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: Frontier developers should argue convincingly that threat actors won't gain significantly increased ability to cause the described catastrophic harm.

locator: Table / Novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those from the previous row, but to a higher standard—to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: Similar but stronger measures than the prior row are needed, sufficient to resist even well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen/modified weights.

locator: Table / Novel chemical/biological weapons production / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Novel chemical/biological weapons production. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: This would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4, but it depends on the capabilities of the strongest and most plausible threat actors that are not bound by a credible governance regime enforcing the recommendations for industry-wide safety outlined here.
paraphrase: This implies security roughly at RAND SL4, contingent on the capabilities of the strongest plausible unbound threat actors.

locator: Table / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: AI systems that are highly relied on and have extensive access to sensitive assets as well as moderate capacity for autonomous, goal-directed operation and subterfuge—such that it is plausible these AI systems could (if directed toward this goal, either deliberately or inadvertently) carry out sabotage leading to irreversibly and substantially higher odds of a later global catastrophe.
paraphrase: This threshold covers AI systems highly relied upon with sensitive access and moderate autonomous/subterfuge capacity, plausibly able to cause sabotage that raises catastrophe odds irreversibly.

locator: Table / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: In the near term, this possibility will likely be most applicable to AI systems that are extensively used within major AI companies, with the opportunity to manipulate how their successor systems are trained and deployed as well as the evidence used to assess their safety.
paraphrase: In the near term, this threshold applies mainly to AI systems used within major AI companies that could manipulate successor training, deployment, or safety evidence.

locator: Table / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: Down the line, this possibility may come to apply to AI systems deployed within government and other high-stakes settings.
paraphrase: Longer term, this threshold could extend to AI systems deployed in government and other high-stakes settings.

context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We will detail the state of our AI systems' capabilities and propensities, our monitoring practices, and the overall level of risk in our Risk Reports.
paraphrase: Anthropic will report on AI capabilities/propensities, monitoring practices, and overall risk level in Risk Reports.

locator: Table / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We expect to continually be able to meet the criteria in the right column, although we cannot make guarantees about an evolving technology that may increasingly have the ability to detect and manipulate testing.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to continually meet the industry-wide criteria but cannot guarantee this as technology evolves to potentially detect/manipulate testing.

context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that AI systems will not carry out sabotage leading to irreversibly and substantially higher odds of a later global catastrophe.
paraphrase: Frontier developers should argue convincingly that their AI systems won't cause sabotage that irreversibly raises catastrophe odds.

locator: Table / High-stakes sabotage opportunities / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: This case may initially be relatively simple and rely heavily on capability limitations, if it is first required when the risk is merely plausible.
paraphrase: The initial safety case may be simple and rely on capability limits when the risk is only plausible.

context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:

context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:

context_stem: Row: High-stakes sabotage opportunities. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. As risk becomes harder to rule out, this case will likely include some combination of:

paraphrase: Recommended measure: capability assessments showing models cannot carry out irreversible, unnoticed sabotage.

paraphrase: Recommended measure: evidence showing models lack deceptive, manipulative, or sabotaging tendencies toward users.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: AI systems that can fully automate, or otherwise dramatically accelerate, the work of large, top-tier teams of human researchers in domains where fast progress could cause threats to international security and/or rapid disruptions to the global balance of power—for example, energy, robotics, weapons development and AI itself.
paraphrase: This threshold covers AI systems that can fully automate or dramatically accelerate top-tier R&D teams in domains threatening international security or global power balance.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: For now, our evaluations will focus specifically on AI R&D, as this domain likely plays to AI systems' current strengths and is more tractable to assess than capabilities in other domains.
paraphrase: Evaluations currently focus on AI R&D because it suits current AI strengths and is easier to assess than other domains.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: Additionally, AI R&D alone could cause acceleration in AI capabilities improvements, to the point where all of the threats listed above (and more) develop very quickly.
paraphrase: AI R&D acceleration alone could rapidly worsen all previously listed threats.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: We will consider this threshold to be met if we determine that either (1) our models would be able to fully substitute for our entire set of Research Scientists and Research Engineers, at competitive costs (i.e., within a factor of 5); or (2) there is "dramatic acceleration" of the pace of AI progress for reasons that likely relate to the automation of AI R&D.
paraphrase: The threshold is met if models could fully replace all Research Scientists/Engineers at competitive cost (within 5x), or if AI-driven R&D automation causes dramatic acceleration.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: We would consider scenario (2) to have occurred where (a) we observe or expect double the rate of progress in AI aggregate capabilities compared to the rate we'd expect in the absence of significant AI contributions to AI R&D and (b) it is plausible that this doubling is substantially attributable to the automation of research and/or engineering (as opposed to other factors, such as increased headcount, compute, or general productivity), such that continuation of the trend in AI progress could lead to even greater acceleration.
paraphrase: Scenario (2) requires observing double the expected AI capability progress rate attributable substantially to R&D automation rather than other factors, with potential for further acceleration.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: This capability threshold is intended to reflect our definition of highly capable models (see Section 3.6).
paraphrase: This threshold is meant to align with the document's definition of highly capable models in Section 3.6.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Capability or usage threshold
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Capability or usage threshold.
excerpt: It may be sensible to add earlier, and/or easier-to-measure, thresholds that trigger less demanding versions of the mitigations for this threshold.
paraphrase: Additional earlier or easier-to-measure thresholds triggering lighter mitigations may be added.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / footnote 4
excerpt: "Double the rate of progress" means "as much progress in one year as one would see in two years at baseline."
paraphrase: Footnote defines double the rate of progress as one year's progress equaling two baseline years.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / footnote 4
excerpt: For example, if baseline progress involved a 3x scaleup in compute and a 3x improvement in algorithmic efficiency (for a 9x "effective scaleup"), "double the rate of progress" would entail something like an 81x effective scaleup.
paraphrase: Footnote example: baseline 9x effective scaleup would become roughly 81x under the doubled-progress definition.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / footnote 4
excerpt: This is not the same idea as "doubling researchers' productivity," since doubling inputs does not necessarily double the rate of progress.
paraphrase: Footnote clarifies that doubled progress rate is distinct from doubled researcher productivity, since input doubling doesn't guarantee doubled progress.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We will:
paraphrase: Lead-in to a list of company commitments for this threshold.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Resource and complete significant "moonshot R&D for security" projects, to explore ambitious and possibly unconventional ways to achieve unprecedented levels of security against the world's best-resourced attackers.
paraphrase: Anthropic will fund and complete ambitious 'moonshot' security R&D projects aiming for unprecedented protection against top-tier attackers.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Achieve an "eyes on everything" state for our internal AI development.
paraphrase: Anthropic will achieve full visibility ('eyes on everything') over internal AI development.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: We will comprehensively gather, centralize, and maintain logs for all critical AI-development activities, and use AI to analyze them for issues including security threats, concerning behavior by insiders (humans as well as AI systems themselves), and training processes or data that are out of line with the public Constitution that shapes and defines our AI models.
paraphrase: Anthropic will comprehensively log critical AI-development activities and use AI to analyze them for security threats, insider concerns (human or AI), and misalignment with the public Constitution.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Perform systematic alignment assessments to examine Claude's behavioral patterns and propensities, meaningfully incorporating mechanistic interpretability and adversarial red-teaming to test our auditing methods.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct systematic alignment assessments of Claude's behavior using mechanistic interpretability and adversarial red-teaming.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 4
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Develop our internal red-teaming of our deployment safeguards to the point where our internal red-teaming performs better at finding potential jailbreaks than the collective abilities of the participants in our established bug bounty programs.
paraphrase: Anthropic will strengthen internal red-teaming until it outperforms the combined efforts of its bug bounty program participants at finding jailbreaks.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company / bullet 5
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company. We will:
excerpt: Publish Risk Reports with the status of, and noteworthy findings from, all of the above, subject to external review by at least one expert, experienced, credible, candid and disinterested external party.
paraphrase: Anthropic will publish Risk Reports on the status/findings of these efforts, subject to review by at least one qualified independent external party.
stated_bar: at least one expert, experienced, credible, candid and disinterested external party

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—our plan as a company
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—our plan as a company.
excerpt: We broadly expect to lead the industry in practices that reduce the risks from AI, although we cannot unilaterally make guarantees about the safety level of AI this advanced.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects to lead the industry in risk-reducing practices but cannot unilaterally guarantee safety at this advanced capability level.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
excerpt: A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
paraphrase: Lead-in to a list of arguments frontier developers should make for this threshold.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: No user or team of users (including those backed by top-tier states) will become significantly more likely to cause catastrophic harm via their usage of product surfaces or via theft of model weights.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: no user or team, even state-backed, gains significantly increased ability to cause catastrophic harm via product use or weight theft.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed in row 1, but to a higher standard‚ to the point where even well-resourced and -staffed threat actors would be unlikely to reliably jailbreak models or cause catastrophic harm via unauthorized access to or modification of models (including via stolen or modified model weights).
paraphrase: This requires row-1-type measures at a higher standard sufficient to resist well-resourced threat actors from jailbreaking or misusing stolen/modified weights.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Accomplishing this would likely mean security roughly in line with RAND SL4. Security requirements would be calibrated to defend against the strongest plausible threat actors who are not bound by a credible industry-wide safety regime.
paraphrase: This implies security roughly at RAND SL4, calibrated against the strongest plausible unbound threat actors.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 1
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Actors subject to such a regime would not need to be treated as threats to each other's model weights.
paraphrase: Developers under a credible industry-wide regime would not need to treat each other as weight-theft threats.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: Even malicious employees and other insiders with maximal levels of access will not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: even maximally privileged malicious insiders would not be significantly enabled to cause catastrophic harm.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This requires (among other things) accounting for internal tools that are less restricted than product surfaces, and for the possibility of unauthorized modification of models.
paraphrase: This requires accounting for less-restricted internal tools and the possibility of unauthorized model modification.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 2
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require an internal Usage Policy and strong internal compartmentalization, controls and/or monitoring to restrict the ability of employees and contractors (up to and including the company's CEO as well as its most privileged technical employees) to circumvent the Usage Policy.
paraphrase: This likely requires an internal Usage Policy plus strong compartmentalization/controls/monitoring restricting even the CEO and top technical staff from circumventing it.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: AI models have not been deliberately or inadvertently trained with dangerous goals, or are otherwise unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Recommended argument: models have not been trained (deliberately or inadvertently) with dangerous goals and are unlikely to autonomously cause catastrophic harm.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: This will likely require similar measures to those listed above under "High-stakes sabotage opportunities" (some combination of internal compartmentalization, restriction and code review; monitoring AI behavior; and evidence that AI models lack the propensity to deceive and manipulate users), but to a greater degree.
paraphrase: This requires similar but stronger measures to those under high-stakes sabotage: compartmentalization, monitoring, and evidence against deceptive/manipulative propensities.

locator: Table / Automated R&D in key domains / Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations / bullet 3
context_stem: Row: Automated R&D in key domains. Column: Mitigations—ambitious industry-wide recommendations. A frontier developer should make a strong argument that:
excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.
paraphrase: Because AI may generate much of the risk-assessment evidence and could be capable of deception/manipulation, threat analyses should apply very high evidentiary standards accounting for possible evidence manipulation.

excerpt: We will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap laying out ambitious but achievable goals for improving our risk mitigations—charting our progress as a company and raising the bar over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap with ambitious, achievable goals that track and raise the bar on risk mitigation progress.

excerpt: Maintaining and reporting on this Roadmap is part of our work under the RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap maintenance and reporting are part of the RSP's obligations.

excerpt: It will be shared with all full-time employees as well as our Board of Directors (Board) and Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), and published in redacted form.
paraphrase: The Roadmap will be shared internally with all full-time employees, the Board, and the LTBT, and published externally in redacted form.

excerpt: We will provide updates on whether we achieve the goals, and set new goals when we do.
paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals as achieved.

excerpt: Our Frontier Safety Roadmap is subject to change.
paraphrase: The Roadmap can change over time.

excerpt: Some changes may simply reflect our evolving understanding of how best to mitigate key risks.
paraphrase: Changes to the Roadmap may reflect evolving understanding of risk mitigation.

excerpt: However, we will strive to avoid situations where we revise the goals in a less ambitious direction simply because we are unable to achieve them.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening Roadmap goals merely due to an inability to meet them.

excerpt: By establishing this expectation, we hope to create a forcing function for work that would otherwise be challenging to appropriately prioritize and resource, as it requires collaboration (and in some cases sacrifices) from multiple parts of the company and can be at cross-purposes with immediate competitive and commercial priorities.
paraphrase: This expectation is meant to force prioritization of cross-company collaborative work that might otherwise conflict with competitive/commercial priorities.

excerpt: Publishing our Frontier Safety Roadmap may also help inform broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.
paraphrase: Publishing the Roadmap may also contribute to broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.

excerpt: Our current Frontier Safety Roadmap is available at anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy/roadmap.
paraphrase: The current Roadmap is published at a specified Anthropic URL.

excerpt: We will also keep past Roadmaps available at that link.
paraphrase: Past versions of the Roadmap will remain accessible at the same link.
